target_customer: Retail investors in Latin America, starting with Brazil, who want to buy US stocks and ETFs cheaply and learn from other investors
problem: Latin Americans had little access to US markets with small amounts and low fees, and investing advice was fragmented, so the founders paired fractional US investing with a social layer to learn and share ideas.
business_model: Brokerage platform with fractional US stocks and ETFs from 1 dollar and no account minimums or fees, monetized later through the brokerage relationship and services
product_category: Fintech, social investing and brokerage app

founders.name: Tyler Richie
education: Left a computer science masters program
founders.background_notes: First data scientist at Nubank as it grew from about 30 to 1,500 employees, then tech lead at a blockchain startup in Singapore, per the YC page. Described as an American who had lived and worked in Brazil.

founders.name: Ruben Guerrero
founders.background_notes: American who had lived and worked in Brazil per Brazilian press; the YC page gives no further details.

competitors.name: Avenue
competitors.what: Full service platform for Brazilians to invest in US stocks, tied to Itau

competitors.name: Stake
competitors.what: Platform giving Brazilians access to US stocks

competitors.name: Passfolio
competitors.what: US investing access app with a large Brazilian user base

competitors.name: Nomad
competitors.what: Brazilian neobank offering US investing access

technical_complexity.rationale: Built a brokerage app on a partner broker (Alpaca at the 2021 stage, DriveWealth by 2022) plus social features. The hard parts were compliance and licensing in Brazil, not core software.

defensibility.rationale: Several established competitors offered similar US access, fees were driven toward zero, and the social layer only worked with a large user base, so copying was easy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept scale. Sproutfi bought Passfolio's Brazilian client portfolio in October 2022 and then combined with Vest, which kept the Vest brand and CEO.

market_need_then: Brazilians were already buying US stocks through Avenue, Stake, Passfolio and Nomad, which showed demand, and the founders expected multiple winners. Brazilian launch depended on legal steps in 2021.

branding.domain_note: The YC listing shows no website, so no domain data was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline Learn. Share. Invest. with a community and education tone

rebrands.why: Vest CEO said many Brazilian users did not know what sprout means and that vest better alludes to investing, per a Brazilian trade article.

brand_strength.rationale: A growth metaphor name that the merged company's CEO said Brazilian users did not understand, and the brand was retired within about two years.

outcome_analysis: Sproutfi, led by a former early Nubank data scientist, raised about 5.7 million dollars in 2021 to offer fractional US investing and a social network for Latin Americans, in a market where Avenue, Stake, Passfolio and Nomad were already established. It bought Passfolio's Brazilian client book in 2022, then combined with Vest, whose CEO retained leadership and later phased out the Sprout name, which he said Brazilian users did not understand.
notes: Directory status is Acquired; the transaction is described as a merger or joining of forces with Vest, with the exit date July 2023 from Dealroom and Seedtable while one Portuguese article may be dated 2024, so the date is uncertain. The seed was raised in two tranches around April and August 2021 per the article, shown as 2021-09 from the article date; seed total of 5.7 million dollars also appears on one aggregator. The 990K November 2022 round is from CB Insights only and unverified, kept because the amount and investor match a separate aggregator listing. Confidence labeled high because founders, competition and funding each have a source, though funding totals vary by aggregator (5.5 to 6.82 million). YC listing has no website so no site fetch was possible; Brazilian launch status in 2021 depended on regulatory steps. The failure_factors list is a judgment from thin evidence.
